plan.title: bug(gates): a brief stranded in active/ by one merge reddens the merge gate on every other open PR

narratives.Description: bug(gates): a brief stranded in active/ by one merge reddens the merge gate on every other open PR
narratives.Overview:
## The defect

`verify:orphan-active` sits in both `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` and `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES`, and `evaluate.ts` enumerates every running brief under `xbrief/active/` with no diff ownership. One brief stranded by any merge therefore fails the merge gate on every other open PR, naming a file those PRs never touched.

Measured 2026-08-28: PRs #3879, #3883, #3887 and #3889 failed the same two lanes at 21:14 on this verifier. #3879 then passed a re-run with its head unchanged once the strandings landed. Two single-brief lifecycle PRs each removed one stranded brief and neither could pass alone, because each still evaluated the other's; a third PR had to carry both. Six occurrences in one day across two independent agents (comment 5458453552).

The deadlock is structural: a repo-wide predicate evaluated per PR means k open PRs go red for one stranded file, and n strandings mutually block their own n cleanups.

## The sharper finding, from the critic

`orphan-active` decides a linked PR shipped by reading REST `merged_at`. During a candidate's own merge gate the candidate is not merged, so its `merged_at` is null. The gate cannot detect the residue the candidate is about to create. It detects debt already in the base, or an issue closed earlier. So the repo-wide scan has no unique preventive value for the PR under test: it fails to stop the merge that creates the debt and then blocks unrelated PRs after the debt exists.

## Two refuted arguments, recorded so they are not retried

1. The `verify:completed-tracked` merge-gate exclusion is NOT precedent. That exclusion exists to avoid deadlocking in-flight lifecycle PRs, and the two checks key on different state: `orphan-active` keys on issue closure AND linked-PR `merged_at`; `completed-tracked` treats an open issue as nonterminal and asks whether a tracked terminal artifact exists on the delivery tip.
2. "Master state is truthful" does not justify giving an unrelated PR merge authority over another agent's residue.

## Design

Scope the merge-chokepoint run to diff ownership; keep the detector semantics untouched.

- New `verify:orphan-active --changed-only [--base-ref <ref>]`. The active/running scan is restricted to briefs the candidate's own diff touches, computed as `git diff --name-only <merge-base>..HEAD` limited to the lifecycle `active/` prefix.
- When HEAD is an ancestor of the base ref there is no candidate diff, so the full repo-wide sweep runs. That is the delivery-tip enforcement: master's own `check:merge` and every push-to-master run keep repo-wide truth.
- Base ref resolution: explicit `--base-ref`, else `origin/<plan.policy.deliveryBranch>`, else the local delivery branch. An unresolvable base ref falls back to the repo-wide sweep and says so, so the flag can never silently narrow the scan.
- `assessOrphanSignature` is unchanged, so the linked-PR/open-issue signature is preserved on every path. No #3156 retirement is required.
- Bare `verify:orphan-active` stays repo-wide: `deft doctor`, manual runs, swarm finalize, and the post-merge `--issue N` DONE gate (#3429) are unaffected.

## Named check-composition change (#3156 / #3145)

The merge chokepoint moves from the unscoped form to `verify:orphan-active --changed-only` on `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES`, `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES`, `check:framework-source` and `check:consumer`. The gate id is unchanged, so it stays on both lists and every gate-integrity test still resolves it.

`verify:consumer-check-contract` is updated in the same change to know about the scoped form: a new `MERGE_CHOKEPOINT_SCOPED_GATE_ARGS` record names each gate that must carry a scoping argument on a check aggregate, and the contract reports an aggregate that composes the unscoped form. Framework source fails closed on it; consumer deposits warn while `deft update` re-deposits the Taskfile. This is strictly additive: no gate definition, verifier, required check, coverage floor, or policy flag is weakened.

No repo-wide scan is added to any merge chokepoint. The existing pre-merge preventive signal for closeout residue remains `verify:pr-closeout-attestable` (#3781), which keys on the PR's structured closing references rather than the branch diff and runs as the last gate before the merge call.

## Unresolved, deliberately (carried from the issue)

Whether the pre-merge run has ever uniquely caught residue a delivery-tip check would have missed is unresolved. The design is safe under both answers: the signature is preserved rather than retired, and the repo-wide sweep still runs at the delivery tip and after merge.
